additional_concerns: The executable answers whether an applicable paragraph 14 demonstration request exists, using a supplied classification. It does not establish that a request was actually made, that demonstration is complete, or that substantive duties have been fulfilled.

Paragraph 14 expressly conditions demonstration on request while leaving confirmation unconditional. Footnote 5 can naturally elaborate that demonstration's minimum content, but its unqualified wording also supports a rival independent demonstration expectation. A FALSE result must remain confined to the declared request-conditioned reading.
SFC satisfaction and high confidence concern assurance standards, not whether a request occurred. Their broader attachment remains unresolved; the formula does not adjudicate it.

Paragraph 16's legal-opinion request is distinct from paragraph 14's demonstration request and paragraph 15's audit request. A communication may contain multiple requests, but one request must not automatically substitute for another.

The supplied intermediary paragraphs 17–18 impose activity-conditioned due diligence and understanding of controls. They neither establish a paragraph 14 request nor automatically apply to every Product Provider. Their referenced Appendix Parts A and B are absent.

Complete paragraphs 10–13, footnote 2 and applicable Appendix factors are needed for a comprehensive substantive compliance assessment. Their absence does not itself prevent answering the narrow request-occurrence question.

No unsupported additional executable restriction or permission is apparent within the declared question. TRUE_IS_SATISFIED must be understood as satisfaction of the request condition, not discharge of the demonstration duty. Structural tool results establish no legal premise.
